purpose: Stamatatos (2017) text-distortion distance to a baseline. Masks every word outside the shared function-word list (or the baseline's top-k words), letter by letter (dv-ma, default) or one asterisk per word (dv-sa), turns digits to #, and keeps punctuation. Character 3-gram profiles of the masked target and baseline are compared by cosine distance over the most frequent baseline n-grams, pooled and per target document. With three or more baseline documents it adds a leave-one-out spread and a percentile for the target, and it lists the masked n-grams that differ most. Baseline documents identical to a target document are excluded. Stdlib only. Descriptive: says how close the masked structure is, not who wrote it.
use_when: You want a topic-light structural distance from a draft or a model's output to an author or register baseline
You want to know whether a rewrite moved function-word placement, word-length rhythm and punctuation toward a target style
You want the text-distortion member of a style panel beside voice_distance (function-word Delta, POS n-grams)
do_not_use_when: You want an authorship or AI-provenance call
You want to check content or fidelity (masking removes it)
The target is under 300 words or the baseline under 1,000 words (it abstains)

inputs.target: text file, directory of .txt/.md, or JSONL with a text field (and optional id)
inputs.baseline: author or register baseline in the same formats

artifacts: results.text_distortion: distance, per_document, baseline_leave_one_out, target_over_baseline, target_under_baseline

compute.cost_note: Pure-Python masking and character n-gram counting; leave-one-out is linear in baseline documents.

examples.description: Distance of one draft to an author baseline directory
Per-item distances for many model outputs, single-asterisk masking, baseline top-200 words kept

references: Stamatatos, E. (2017). Authorship Attribution Using Text Distortion. EACL 2017: https://aclanthology.org/E17-1107/
